questions.question: What do you call an event where a computer becomes unresponsive due to either a program or the system itself becoming unresponsive and no longer taking input?
questions.questionHtml: What do you call an event where a computer becomes unresponsive due to either a program or the system itself becoming unresponsive and no longer taking input?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hanging.

Key Points

  • A hang is an event where a computer becomes unresponsive due to either a program or the system itself becoming unresponsive and no longer taking input.
    • It is a blanket term for unresponsiveness, be it a small application or process, the operating system itself or a piece of hardware being unresponsive.
    • Hangs have a variety of causes, from software encountering an error that it cannot handle, simple lack of resources, which means the system is just waiting, to more serious systemic problems such as driver incompatibility or hardware malfunction.
    • Most hangs are minor and usually resolve themselves, especially if it is only a resource issue, meaning it only appears to be hung because it is waiting for a resource such as memory or CPU time.

Additional Information

  • With removable disk drives, eject means to disengage the medium (removable disk) so it may be removed. 
  • The operating system completes any read or write operations on the drive, and unmounts it from the computer.
  • With computers, to move is to permanently transfer text, data, or files from one location to another without duplicating them.
  • In computing, booting is the process of starting a computer.

questions.question: An/A ______ is a finite set of instructions which, when followed, accomplish a particular task.
questions.questionHtml: An/A ______ is a finite set of instructions which, when followed, accomplish a particular task.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is algorithm.

Key Points

  • An algorithm is a finite set of instructions that, if followed, accomplishes a particular task.
  • It is the step by step procedure for solving any problem.
  • Algorithms are used to specify how calculations, data processing, automated reasoning, automated decision-making, and other tasks should be carried out.
  • All algorithms must meet the following requirements:
    • The inputs to an algorithm can be zero or more and come from a specific set of objects.
    • An algorithm has one or more outputs that are related to the inputs in some way.
    • Each step must be properly stated, and each instruction must be concise and clear.
    • After a finite number of steps, the algorithm must always end.
    • All operations must be sufficiently fundamental to be completed precisely and in a finite amount of time.

questions.question: How many terabytes make one petabyte?
questions.questionHtml: How many terabytes make one petabyte?
questions.solution: One petabyte (PB) is equivalent to 1024 terabytes (TB). This follows the binary system used in computing where each higher unit of measurement is 1024 times the previous unit. Hence, 1 PB = 1024 TB.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary storage device in a personal computer?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a primary storage device in a personal computer?
questions.solution: Primary storage, also known as main storage or memory, is the main area in a computer where data is stored for quick access by the processor. In personal computers, this is typically referred to as random access memory (RAM). RAM is directly attached to the CPU, differentiating it from secondary storage devices like hard disks, diskettes, CDs, and DVDs, which are not directly connected to the CPU. Storage devices are used for saving, carrying, and retrieving data and can be internal or external to a computer or server. Examples include pen drives, hard disks, and compact disks.

questions.question: Second generation computers (1955-1964) were made of:
questions.questionHtml: Second generation computers (1955-1964) were made of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is transistors.

  • Second-generation computers (1955-1964) were made of transistors.​

Key Points

  • Vacuum tube – an electronic device that controls the flow of electrons in a vacuum. It is used as a switch, amplifier, or display screen in many older model radios, televisions, computers, etc.
  • Transistor – an electronic component that can be used as an amplifier or as a switch. It is used to control the flow of electricity in radios, televisions, computers, etc.
  • Integrated circuit (IC) – a small electronic circuit printed on a chip (usually made of silicon) that contains many its own circuit elements (e.g. transistors, diodes, resistors, etc.).
  • Microprocessor – an electronic component held on an integrated circuit that contains a computer’s central processing unit (CPU) and other associated circuits.

Important Points

Five Generations of Computers

Generations of computers Evolving hardware
First-generation Vacuum tube
Second generation Transistor
Third generation Integrated circuit
Fourth generation Microprocessor
Fifth-generation Artificial intelligence

questions.question: What is the other name for 'transistor computer'?
questions.questionHtml: What is the other name for 'transistor computer'?
questions.solution: Second-generation computers, spanning from 1959 to 1965, are also known as transistor computers, as they replaced vacuum tubes with transistors. This period marked significant advancements in computing technology, leading to more reliable and efficient machines. The generations of computers are categorized as follows: First Generation (1946-1954) used Vacuum Tubes, Second Generation (1955-1964) used Transistors, Third Generation (1964-1977) used Integrated Circuits, Fourth Generation (1978-Present) uses VLSI or Microprocessors, and the Fifth Generation (Present and Future) focuses on ULSI or Bio-Chips. These transitions highlight the evolution and miniaturization of electronic components in computing.

questions.question: ______ is an interpreted, high-level and general-purpose programming language.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is an interpreted, high-level and general-purpose programming language.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Python.

  • Python is an interpreted, object-oriented, high-level programming language with dynamic semantics.
    • Its high-level data structure, coupled with dynamic typing and dynamic binding, make it very attractive for rapid application development as well as for use as a scripting or glue language for linking existing components together.
    • Python's simple, easy-to-learn syntax emphasizes readability and therefore reduces program maintenance costs.
    • Python supports modules and packages, which encourage program modularity and code reuse.

Additional Information

  • Different Types of Computer Language
    • Machine Language
      • The machine language is sometimes referred to as machine code or object code which is set of binary digits 0 and 1. These binary digits are understood and read by a computer system and interpret easily.
      • It is considered a native language as it can be directly understood by a central processing unit (CPU).
    • Assembly Language
      • The assembly language is considered a low-level language for microprocessors and many other programmable devices.
      • The assembly language is also considered a second-generation language.
      • The first generation language is machine language.
    • High-Level Language
      • The development of high-level language was done when the programmers face the issue in writing programs as the older language has portability issues which means the code written in one machine cannot be transferred to other machines.

questions.question: In the context of computing, a byte is equal to ______ bits.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 8.

Key Points

  • A byte consists of 8 binary digits (bits), each of which consists of a 0 or 1. A single byte can be used to represent 28 or 256 different values.
  • The byte was basically created to store a single character, since 256 values is sufficient to represent all lowercase and uppercase letters, numbers, and symbols in western languages.
  • Nibble: Collection of 4 bits.
  • Word: Collection of 2 Bytes.

It has become a fundamental unit of measurement for data storage.

1 KB 1024 Bytes
1 MB 1024 KB
1 GB 1024 MB

questions.question: A computer on the Internet that uses HTTP protocol is known as:
questions.questionHtml: A computer on the Internet that uses HTTP protocol is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Web Server.

Key Points

  • A computer on the Internet that uses HTTP protocol is known as a Web Server.
    • The Hypertext Transfer Protocol is an application protocol for distributed, collaborative, hypermedia information systems that allow users to communicate data on the World Wide Web.
    • Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is a method for encoding and transporting information between a client and a web server.
    • HTTP is the primary protocol for the transmission of information across the Internet.
    • The primary function of HTTP is to establish a connection with the server and send HTML pages back to the user's browser.
      • The browser adds the rest.

Additional Information

  •  LAN:
    • A local area network (LAN) is a collection of devices connected together in one physical location, such as a building, office, or home.
    • A LAN can be small or large, ranging from a home network with one user to an enterprise network with thousands of users and devices in an office or school.
      • PCs/workstations and servers.
      • Network Interface Card (NIC).
      • Cabling and connectors, for example, coaxial cable and BNC connector, Unshielded Twisted Pair (UTP) and RJ-45 connector.
      • Hub, concentrator, and more complicated network devices such as Bridge, LAN Switch and Router.
  • WAN:
    • A wide area network is a telecommunications network that extends over a large geographic area for the primary purpose of computer networking.
    • Wide area networks are often established with leased telecommunication circuits.
    • The WAN allows the router to connect to the internet and share that connection with all the Ethernet-ready devices connected to it.

questions.question: Of the units mentioned in the options, which one is the largest as compared to the others?
questions.questionHtml: Of the units mentioned in the options, which one is the largest as compared to the others?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tera.

Key Points

  • Of the units mentioned in the options, Tera is the largest as compared to the others.
  • A computer processor is made up of multiple decisive circuits, each one of which may be either OFF or ON.
  • These two states in terms of memory are represented by a 0 or 1.
    • In order to count higher than 1, such bits (BInary digiTS) are suspended together.
    • A group of eight bits is known as a byte.
    • 1 byte can represent numbers between zero (00000000) and 255 (11111111), or 28 = 256 distinct positions. Of course, these bytes may also be combined to represent larger numbers.
  • Types of various Units of Memory based on size:
    • Byte
    • KiloByte
    • MegaByte
    • GigaByte
    • TeraByte
    • Peta Byte
    • Exa Byte
    • Zetta Byte
    • Yotta Byte

Additional Information

  • The memory of a Computer is any physical device that is capable of storing information whether it is large or small and stores it temporarily or permanently.
    • For example, Random Access Memory (RAM), is a type of volatile memory that stores information for a short interval of time, on an integrated circuit used by the operating system. 
    • Memory can be either volatile or non-volatile.
    • Volatile memory is a type of memory that loses its contents when the computer or hardware device is switched off.

questions.question: The Computer Technology is based on which of the following scientific principals?
questions.questionHtml: The Computer Technology is based on which of the following scientific principals?

options.text: Light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation
options.html: Light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation

questions.solution: Computer Technology relies on Digital logic principles, which involve the combination of binary values through printed circuit board technology. This includes the use of circuits and five essential logic gates: AND, OR, XOR, NAND, and NOR. Superconductivity, characterized by zero electrical resistance at very low temperatures, and the photoelectric effect, the emission of electrons upon light exposure, are not foundational to computer technology. Digital logic is crucial for implementing computer operations, distinguishing it as the core principle behind modern computing systems.

questions.question: A _________ is one billionth of a metre.
questions.questionHtml: A _________ is one billionth of a metre.
questions.solution: A nanometre (nm) is one billionth of a metre, commonly used in physics, chemistry, and nanotechnology to measure extremely small lengths. In contrast, a parsec is an astronomical unit equivalent to about 3.26 light-years. A micrometre (µm) is one millionth of a metre, used in biology and materials science. An angstrom (Å) is one ten-billionth of a metre, used to measure atomic and molecular scales. Each unit serves distinct purposes based on the scale and field of study, from measuring astronomical distances to observing microscopic and atomic dimensions.

questions.question: Which technology is commonly used for sending and receiving electronic mail?
questions.questionHtml: Which technology is commonly used for sending and receiving electronic mail?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Internet and email protocols.

Key Points

  • TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol.
  • The Internet protocol suite is the conceptual model and set of communications protocols used in the Internet and similar computer networks.
  • It is commonly known as TCP/IP because the foundational protocols in the suite are the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and the Internet Protocol (IP). 

Additional Information

  • Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is an application-layer protocol for transmitting hypermedia documents, such as HTML.
  • SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. 
  • The File Transfer Protocol (FTP) is a standard communication protocol used for the transfer of computer files from a server to a client on a computer network.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of network that allows users from outside to access the Intranet of an organisation?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a type of network that allows users from outside to access the Intranet of an organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Extranet.

Key Points

  • An Extranet is a private network that leverages internet technology and the public telecommunication system to securely share part of a business's information or operations with suppliers, vendors, partners, customers, or other businesses.
  • It allows controlled access to the organization's internal information from outside the organization's intranet.
  • Extranets improve efficiency by providing a secure environment to exchange data, manage projects, and collaborate with external stakeholders.
  • Security measures such as encryption, user authentication, and firewalls are typically employed to ensure that the data shared over an Extranet remains secure.

Additional Information

  • Intranet:
    • An Intranet is a private network accessible only to an organization's staff.
    • It is used to share company information and computing resources among employees.
    • Intranets improve communication, collaboration, and efficiency within an organization.
  • Internet:
    • The Internet is a global network of interconnected computers that communicate freely and share information worldwide.
    • It is publicly accessible and used for a variety of purposes, including communication, research, and commerce.
  • Virtual Private Network (VPN):
    • A VPN creates a secure, encrypted connection over a less secure network, such as the internet.
    • It enables users to send and receive data as if their devices were directly connected to the private network.
  • Firewall:
    • A firewall is a network security device that monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on an organization's previously established security policies.
    • It acts as a barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external networks, such as the internet.

questions.question: Autocorrect function may be used in MS Word 365, for grammar and spell-check and it is available through:
questions.questionHtml: Autocorrect function may be used in MS Word 365, for grammar and spell-check and it is available through:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is File → Options → Proofing.

Key Points

  • The Autocorrect function in MS Word 365 is used for grammar and spell-check to enhance document accuracy.
  • This feature can be accessed via the path: File → Options → Proofing in MS Word 365.
  • Under the Proofing tab, you can customize various autocorrect options to suit your needs.
  • The Proofing options include settings for correcting spelling and grammar in real-time, managing dictionaries, and customizing autocorrect entries.

Additional Information

  • Autocorrect
    • Autocorrect is a software feature that automatically corrects misspelled words and grammatical errors as you type.
    • It can also be customized to include specific words or phrases that you frequently use, enhancing typing efficiency.
  • Proofing Tools
    • Proofing tools in MS Word include spell-check, grammar-check, and thesaurus functions that help improve the quality of your documents.
    • These tools can be accessed under the Proofing tab in the Options menu.
  • Custom Dictionaries
    • MS Word allows users to create custom dictionaries to include specific terms and jargon relevant to their work.
    • This feature ensures that industry-specific terms are not flagged as errors during spell-check.
  • Grammar Settings
    • Under the Proofing options, users can adjust grammar settings to follow different style guides such as APA, MLA, or Chicago.
    • This customization ensures that documents adhere to the required writing standards.

questions.question: In MS Excel 365, which of the following is the correct formula to calculate the average of the values in cells A1 to A10?
questions.questionHtml: In MS Excel 365, which of the following is the correct formula to calculate the average of the values in cells A1 to A10?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is =AVERAGE(A1:A10).

Key Points

  • AVERAGE is a built-in function in MS Excel used to calculate the mean of a group of numbers.
  • The correct formula to calculate the average of values in cells A1 to A10 is =AVERAGE(A1:A10).
  • The AVERAGE function in Excel ignores empty cells and cells that contain text or logical values.
  • Using the AVERAGE function helps in quickly determining the central value of a data set in a spreadsheet.

Additional Information

  • SUM Function
    • The SUM function in Excel is used to add together a series of numbers.
    • The syntax for the SUM function is =SUM(number1, [number2], ...).
    • It is one of the most commonly used functions in Excel for data analysis.
  • COUNT Function
    • The COUNT function in Excel counts the number of cells that contain numbers within a specified range.
    • The syntax for the COUNT function is =COUNT(value1, [value2], ...).
    • This function is useful for quickly determining the number of numerical entries in a data set.
  • IF Function
    • The IF function in Excel performs a logical test and returns one value for a TRUE result and another for a FALSE result.
    • The syntax for the IF function is =IF(logical_test, value_if_true, value_if_false).
    • This function is essential for creating conditional statements in Excel.
  • VLOOKUP Function
    • The VLOOKUP function in Excel searches for a value in the first column of a table array and returns a value in the same row from a specified column.
    • The syntax for the VLOOKUP function is =VLOOKUP(lookup_value, table_array, col_index_num, [range_lookup]).
    • It is widely used for data retrieval and reference tasks in Excel spreadsheets.

questions.question: What does ‘CC’ stand for in the context of email?
questions.questionHtml: What does ‘CC’ stand for in the context of email?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Carbon Copy.

Key Points

  • 'CC' in email stands for Carbon Copy.
  • It is used to send a copy of the email to recipients other than the primary recipient.
  • Recipients listed in the CC field can see who else has received the email.
  • It is typically used to keep individuals informed without requiring them to take any action.

Additional Information

  • BCC (Blind Carbon Copy):
    • This field is used to send a copy of the email to recipients without disclosing their email addresses to the other recipients.
    • It is useful for maintaining the privacy of email addresses.
  • Email Etiquette:
    • Use CC sparingly to avoid overwhelming recipients with unnecessary emails.
    • Ensure that the primary recipient is aware of who is included in the CC field.
  • History of CC:
    • The term originates from the practice of using carbon paper to create copies of documents.
    • In email, it serves a similar function of making copies of the message for additional recipients.
  • Difference Between To, CC, and BCC:
    • To: The primary recipient(s) of the email.
    • CC: Secondary recipients who are visible to all other recipients.
    • BCC: Secondary recipients who are not visible to other recipients.
